items.prompt:
The legitimate right to exercise political power is best described as:

A) Authority
B) Coercion
C) Influence
D) Propaganda

Power that is accepted as rightful by those who are governed is said to possess:

A) Sovereignty
B) Legitimacy
C) Anarchy
D) Bureaucracy

The ability to influence the behaviour of others, with or without their consent, is:

A) Liberty
B) Equality
C) Power
D) Fraternity

Authority based on long-standing customs and inherited position is classified as:

A) Legal authority
B) Charismatic authority
C) Coercive authority
D) Traditional authority

Authority that rests on the exceptional personal qualities of a leader is:

A) Charismatic authority
B) Traditional authority
C) Rational-legal authority
D) Bureaucratic authority

The supreme law-making power of a state within its territory is called:

A) Federalism
B) Sovereignty
C) Devolution
D) Lobbying

Which feature of sovereignty means it cannot be shared or divided?

A) Flexibility
B) Delegation
C) Indivisibility
D) Partition

The location of ultimate political power in the electorate of a democracy is referred to as:

A) Legal sovereignty
B) Internal sovereignty
C) Titular sovereignty
D) Popular sovereignty

Sovereignty that lies with the body legally empowered to make binding laws is:

A) Legal sovereignty
B) Political sovereignty
C) Popular sovereignty
D) External sovereignty

Which of the following is NOT an essential element of a state?

A) Population
B) A political party
C) Territory
D) Government

A defined area of land over which a state exercises control is its:

A) Constitution
B) Manifesto
C) Territory
D) Census

The difference between a nation and a state is that a nation is primarily based on:

A) Armed forces
B) Tax collection
C) Boundary fences
D) Common identity and culture

Government studied as a field of academic enquiry is best described as:

A) A currency
B) A discipline
C) A religion
D) A climate

The continuous process of making and enforcing binding decisions for society describes government as:

A) A souvenir
B) A holiday
C) A process
D) A rumour

The pattern of attitudes and beliefs a people hold toward their political system is their:

A) Gross domestic product
B) Birth rate
C) Trade balance
D) Political culture

A political culture in which citizens are aware of government but largely passive is described as:

A) Subject political culture
B) Participant political culture
C) Parochial political culture
D) Civic incompetence

The process by which individuals acquire political values and attitudes is called:

A) Political apathy
B) Political socialisation
C) Political coercion
D) Political bargaining

A government that came to power through accepted constitutional means is said to have:

A) Illegitimacy
B) Immunity
C) Legitimacy
D) Impunity

The principle that no one is above the law and all are equal before it is the:

A) Rule of thumb
B) Rule of force
C) Rule of secrecy
D) Rule of law

Which of these is a core element of the rule of law?

A) Equality before the law
B) Selective justice
C) Arbitrary arrest
D) Secret trials

The rule of law is most directly undermined when a government practises:

A) Public budgeting
B) Arbitrary detention without trial
C) Judicial review
D) Free elections

The doctrine that the three arms of government should be kept distinct was popularised by:

A) Karl Marx
B) Adam Smith
C) Montesquieu
D) Niccolo Machiavelli

Separation of powers divides government functions among the legislature, judiciary and:

A) Electorate
B) Press
C) Army
D) Executive

The mechanism that allows each arm of government to limit the others is called:

A) Checks and balances
B) Collective bargaining
C) Fiscal federalism
D) Judicial precedent

The duty of citizens to obey the lawful commands of the state is their:

A) Political apathy
B) Political obligation
C) Political asylum
D) Political amnesty

Government of the people, by the people and for the people defines:

A) Oligarchy
B) Monarchy
C) Democracy
D) Theocracy

A democracy in which citizens elect representatives to make laws on their behalf is:

A) Direct democracy
B) Absolute monarchy
C) Military rule
D) Representative democracy

A system in which citizens themselves vote directly on laws and policies is:

A) Direct democracy
B) Indirect democracy
C) Aristocracy
D) Plutocracy

The condition in which citizens enjoy the same rights and opportunities is:

A) Hierarchy
B) Equality
C) Privilege
D) Subjugation

Freedom that requires the absence of external restraint on the individual is termed:

A) Positive freedom
B) Conditional freedom
C) Negative freedom
D) Delegated freedom

Rule by a single person who inherits the throne is known as:

A) Democracy
B) Polyarchy
C) Meritocracy
D) Monarchy

Government by a small privileged group of people is called:

A) Oligarchy
B) Democracy
C) Monarchy
D) Anarchy

A system of government dominated by religious leaders and laws is a:

A) Plutocracy
B) Theocracy
C) Technocracy
D) Bureaucracy

Government by the wealthy class is best described as a:

A) Aristocracy
B) Gerontocracy
C) Plutocracy
D) Meritocracy

A person who legally belongs to a state and enjoys its full rights is a:

A) Tourist
B) Refugee
C) Stateless person
D) Citizen

Citizenship acquired by being born within the territory of a state is by:

A) Birth
B) Bribery
C) Conquest
D) Lottery

The legal process by which a foreigner becomes a citizen of a new country is:

A) Deportation
B) Naturalisation
C) Extradition
D) Repatriation

The claims that citizens can legitimately make on the state are their:

A) Bribes
B) Rumours
C) Rights
D) Hobbies

Paying taxes and obeying the law are examples of a citizen's:

A) Privileges
B) Luxuries
C) Holidays
D) Duties

Rights that belong to all human beings regardless of nationality are called:

A) Fundamental human rights
B) Trade rights
C) Mineral rights
D) Property liens

The right to life and the right to fair hearing are classified as:

A) Economic subsidies
B) Civil rights
C) Customs duties
D) Import quotas

A group of people who share a common history, language and culture form a:

A) Cartel
B) Quorum
C) Nation
D) Census

When several nations are joined under one sovereign state, the state is described as:

A) Mononational
B) Apolitical
C) Acultural
D) Multinational

Voting, joining a party and contesting elections are all forms of:

A) Political participation
B) Political apathy
C) Civil disobedience
D) Tax evasion

The body of fundamental rules by which a state is governed is its:

A) Manifesto
B) Constitution
C) Budget
D) Gazette

A constitution that is contained in a single written document is described as:

A) Unwritten
B) Verbal
C) Written
D) Secret

A constitution drawn from many sources such as conventions and court decisions is:

A) Written
B) Codified
C) Printed
D) Unwritten

A constitution that can be amended only through a special, difficult procedure is:

A) Rigid
B) Flexible
C) Fluid
D) Casual

A constitution that can be changed by the ordinary law-making process is:

A) Rigid
B) Flexible
C) Entrenched
D) Frozen

The British constitution is commonly cited as an example of which type?

A) Written and rigid
B) Codified and rigid
C) Unwritten and flexible
D) Secret and fixed

A clause that is specially protected from easy amendment is said to be:

A) Repealed
B) Suspended
C) Vacated
D) Entrenched

The part of a constitution stating the goals and ideals of the nation is the:

A) Preamble
B) Schedule
C) Appendix
D) Index

The doctrine that the constitution is the highest law of the land is:

A) Parliamentary supremacy
B) Constitutional supremacy
C) Executive supremacy
D) Judicial restraint

Any law that conflicts with a supreme constitution is, to the extent of the conflict:

A) Fully valid
B) Partly binding
C) Null and void
D) Automatically amended

The formal process of changing the provisions of a constitution is called:

A) Dissolution
B) Prorogation
C) Abdication
D) Amendment

mcq_options.text: The legislatures of the component units

items.prompt:
Amending a rigid constitution in a federation often requires the approval of:

A) The legislatures of the component units
B) Only the head of state
C) The armed forces alone
D) Foreign governments
items.correct_answer: A) The legislatures of the component units

items.prompt:
A constitution that shares powers between central and regional governments is:

A) Unitary
B) Federal
C) Confederal in name only
D) Monarchical

A constitution that concentrates power in a single central government is:

A) Federal
B) Confederal
C) Unitary
D) Bicameral

Which of the following is a function of a constitution?

A) Setting market prices
B) Fixing exchange rates
C) Awarding scholarships
D) Defining the powers of government
items.correct_answer: D) Defining the powers of government

items.prompt:
A constitution protects citizens mainly by:

A) Guaranteeing fundamental rights
B) Banning all political parties
C) Abolishing the courts
D) Outlawing elections

The 1946 constitution that introduced regionalism in Nigeria is named after:

A) Clifford
B) Macpherson
C) Richards
D) Lyttleton

The constitution that introduced a federal structure to Nigeria in 1954 is the:

A) Clifford Constitution
B) Richards Constitution
C) Independence Constitution
D) Lyttleton Constitution

The 1979 Nigerian constitution introduced which system of government?

A) Presidential
B) Parliamentary
C) Monarchical
D) Confederal

Statements of national goals not directly enforceable in court are known as:

A) Justiciable rights
B) Fundamental objectives and directive principles
C) Penal codes
D) Tax schedules
items.correct_answer: B) Fundamental objectives and directive principles

items.prompt:
Unwritten practices that are habitually followed in governance are:

A) Statutory instruments
B) Executive orders
C) Constitutional conventions
D) Court injunctions

An advantage of a written constitution is that it:

A) Is easily forgotten
B) Cannot be interpreted
C) Encourages dictatorship
D) Provides a clear reference document
items.correct_answer: D) Provides a clear reference document

mcq_options.text: Is difficult to amend in emergencies

items.prompt:
A common criticism of a rigid constitution is that it:

A) Is difficult to amend in emergencies
B) Changes too often
C) Has no written text
D) Ignores the courts
items.correct_answer: A) Is difficult to amend in emergencies

items.prompt:
A list of citizens' guaranteed liberties within a constitution is a:

A) Bill of exchange
B) Bill of rights
C) Bill of lading
D) Bill of sale

Freedom of expression and freedom of association are usually protected in the:

A) Trade ledger
B) Census record
C) Bill of rights
D) Tax code

The arm of government primarily responsible for interpreting the constitution is the:

A) Legislature
B) Executive
C) Civil service
D) Judiciary

The power of courts to declare laws unconstitutional is known as:

A) Judicial review
B) Legislative veto
C) Executive privilege
D) Royal assent

mcq_options.text: Merging all powers in one office
Separating the powers of the arms of government

items.prompt:
Constitutions promote good governance by clearly:

A) Merging all powers in one office
B) Separating the powers of the arms of government
C) Banning the judiciary
D) Removing all elections
items.correct_answer: B) Separating the powers of the arms of government

items.prompt:
Rules about who qualifies as a citizen are usually contained in the:

A) Weather report
B) Sports calendar
C) Constitution
D) Price list

Special constitutional powers used during war or grave danger are called:

A) Routine powers
B) Ceremonial powers
C) Reserve currency
D) Emergency powers

A constitution mainly establishes the relationship between the government and the:

A) Citizens
B) Weather
C) Ocean
D) Calendar

A confederal constitution gives most reserved powers to the:

A) Central government
B) Component units
C) Monarch
D) Judiciary alone

Under parliamentary supremacy, the highest law-making body is the:

A) Supreme Court
B) Monarch
C) Parliament
D) Electoral commission

A special majority required to amend a rigid constitution is usually:

A) A simple show of hands
B) One member only
C) A foreign vote
D) Two-thirds of the legislature

By limiting the powers of rulers, a constitution helps to prevent:

A) Tyranny
B) Trade
C) Education
D) Agriculture

The constitution under which Nigeria gained independence in 1960 is the:

A) Republican Constitution of 1963
B) Independence Constitution
C) Lyttleton Constitution
D) Richards Constitution

The 1963 constitution made Nigeria a:

A) Monarchy
B) Colony
C) Republic
D) Protectorate

mcq_options.text: A detailed list attached to the main text

items.prompt:
A schedule in a constitution is best described as:

A) A secret memo
B) A foreign treaty
C) A budget speech
D) A detailed list attached to the main text
items.correct_answer: D) A detailed list attached to the main text

items.prompt:
A flexible constitution is praised because it:

A) Adapts easily to changing needs
B) Can never be changed
C) Has no provisions
D) Bans amendments
items.correct_answer: A) Adapts easily to changing needs

items.prompt:
When two laws conflict, a supreme constitution requires courts to uphold the:

A) Older custom
B) Constitution
C) Foreign law
D) Party manifesto

Rights that can be enforced directly in a court of law are described as:

A) Non-justiciable
B) Ceremonial
C) Justiciable
D) Honorary

Directive principles of state policy primarily serve as:

A) Enforceable court orders
B) Tax tables
C) Election results
D) Guides for government policy

Constitutional conventions are binding mainly because of:

A) Long-established practice and acceptance
B) Police enforcement
C) Court fines
D) Foreign treaties

A state of emergency is normally declared by the:

A) A single citizen
B) Executive, subject to legislative approval
C) A foreign embassy
D) A market union
items.correct_answer: B) Executive, subject to legislative approval

items.prompt:
The arm of government responsible for making laws is the:

A) Executive
B) Judiciary
C) Legislature
D) Press

The arm of government that implements and enforces laws is the:

A) Legislature
B) Judiciary
C) Electorate
D) Executive

The arm of government that interprets the law and settles disputes is the:

A) Judiciary
B) Executive
C) Legislature
D) Civil service

Besides making laws, the legislature also performs the function of:

A) Conducting surgery
B) Controlling public finance
C) Building roads directly
D) Trying murder cases

A legislature made up of two chambers is described as:

A) Unicameral
B) Tricameral
C) Bicameral
D) Acameral

A legislature with only one chamber is described as:

A) Bicameral
B) Multicameral
C) Bipartisan
D) Unicameral

The federal legislature of Nigeria is collectively known as the:

A) National Assembly
B) Privy Council
C) Cabinet
D) Supreme Court

The two chambers of Nigeria's National Assembly are the Senate and the:

A) House of Lords
B) House of Representatives
C) House of Chiefs
D) Privy Council

In a presidential system, the head of state is also the:

A) Chief judge
B) Speaker
C) Head of government
D) Auditor

Formulating and implementing government policy is a function of the:

A) Executive
B) Judiciary
C) Press
D) Opposition

The judiciary protects citizens chiefly by:

A) Collecting taxes
B) Safeguarding fundamental rights
C) Printing money
D) Building bridges

The principle that judges should decide cases free from external pressure is:

A) Judicial dependence
B) Executive control
C) Judicial independence
D) Legislative override

Security of tenure for judges helps to guarantee:

A) Higher taxes
B) Faster elections
C) Press freedom
D) Judicial independence

The permanent body of officials that implements government policy is the:

A) Civil service
B) Cabinet
C) Judiciary
D) Legislature

Anonymity and political neutrality are key features of the:

A) Ruling party
B) Civil service
C) Supreme Court
D) Press

mcq_options.text: Remain in office despite changes of government
Serve only one minister for life

items.prompt:
Permanence in the civil service means that officials:

A) Lose jobs after every election
B) Are elected yearly
C) Remain in office despite changes of government
D) Serve only one minister for life
items.correct_answer: C) Remain in office despite changes of government

items.prompt:
State-owned bodies set up to provide essential services are:

A) Private clubs
B) Secret societies
C) Foreign embassies
D) Public corporations

Law made by the executive under powers granted by the legislature is:

A) Delegated legislation
B) Primary legislation
C) Common law
D) Customary law

The legislature checks the executive mainly through its power of:

A) Sentencing criminals
B) Oversight and the budget
C) Hearing appeals
D) Issuing passports

The executive can influence law-making by exercising the power of:

A) Verdict
B) Subpoena
C) Veto
D) Probate

The judiciary checks both other arms through the power of:

A) Tax assessment
B) Conscription
C) Coronation
D) Judicial review

The legislative power to investigate the conduct of public officers is called:

A) Oversight function
B) Pardoning power
C) Appellate function
D) Diplomatic immunity

The power of the executive to grant official forgiveness for an offence is the:

A) Power of veto
B) Prerogative of mercy
C) Power of subpoena
D) Power of audit

The highest court in Nigeria's judicial hierarchy is the:

A) Magistrate Court
B) Customary Court
C) Supreme Court
D) Area Court

Appeals from the Federal High Court in Nigeria first go to the:

A) Supreme Court
B) Magistrate Court
C) Customary Court
D) Court of Appeal

The presiding officer of a House of Representatives is usually the:

A) Speaker
B) Chief Justice
C) Auditor-General
D) Comptroller

The presiding officer of the Senate is the:

A) Speaker
B) Senate President
C) Chief Whip
D) Clerk

The body of senior ministers that advises the head of government is the:

A) Tribunal
B) Jury
C) Cabinet
D) Census board

The career head of a government ministry in many systems is the:

A) Minister
B) Speaker
C) Chief Justice
D) Permanent Secretary

When a court orders the release of a person unlawfully detained, it issues a writ of:

A) Habeas corpus
B) Mandamus only
C) Certiorari only
D) Quo warranto only

Excessive overlap among the arms of government can lead to:

A) Free elections
B) Abuse of power
C) Lower taxes
D) Faster trials

A single member of a law-making house is generally called a:

A) Litigant
B) Defendant
C) Legislator
D) Bailiff

In a parliamentary system, the head of government is usually the:

A) Chief Justice
B) Speaker only
C) Monarch alone
D) Prime Minister

A person who presides over a court and decides cases is a:

A) Judge
B) Legislator
C) Governor
D) Diplomat

mcq_options.text: Provide essential services that private firms may neglect

items.prompt:
A major reason governments establish public corporations is to:

A) Avoid all taxes
B) Provide essential services that private firms may neglect
C) Win football matches
D) Print foreign currency
items.correct_answer: B) Provide essential services that private firms may neglect

items.prompt:
Impartiality in the civil service means officials must serve:

A) Only one political party
B) Foreign donors first
C) Any government in power
D) Their own families

A proposed law being considered by the legislature is called a:

A) Decree
B) Verdict
C) Census
D) Bill

A bill becomes law in a presidential system after it receives:

A) Presidential assent
B) A court verdict
C) A press release
D) A foreign signature

A ceremonial head of state with no real political power is a:

A) Political executive
B) Titular executive
C) Single executive
D) Plural executive

Minor criminal and civil cases are usually first heard in the:

A) Supreme Court
B) Court of Appeal
C) Magistrate Court
D) Senate

Legislative approval of executive appointments is an example of:

A) Judicial precedent
B) Fiscal policy
C) Diplomacy
D) Checks and balances

mcq_options.text: Save legislative time on technical detail

items.prompt:
A common reason for delegated legislation is to:

A) Save legislative time on technical detail
B) Abolish the legislature
C) Replace the courts
D) End all elections
items.correct_answer: A) Save legislative time on technical detail

items.prompt:
Recruitment into the civil service is ideally based on:

A) Bribery
B) Merit
C) Lottery
D) Inheritance

An organised group seeking to control government through elections is a:

A) Trade fair
B) Census board
C) Political party
D) Sports club

mcq_options.text: Select and present candidates for election

items.prompt:
A key function of a political party is to:

A) Try criminal cases
B) Print the constitution
C) Conduct the census
D) Select and present candidates for election
items.correct_answer: D) Select and present candidates for election

items.prompt:
Political parties educate citizens by:

A) Mobilising and informing voters
B) Banning newspapers
C) Closing schools
D) Raising import duties

A political system dominated by only one legal party is a:

A) Two-party system
B) One-party system
C) Multi-party system
D) No-party system

A system in which two major parties realistically compete for power is a:

A) One-party system
B) Multi-party system
C) Two-party system
D) Non-party system

A system with several strong parties competing for power is a:

A) One-party system
B) Two-party system
C) Zero-party system
D) Multi-party system

mcq_options.text: A stable government and clear opposition

items.prompt:
An advantage of a two-party system is that it tends to produce:

A) A stable government and clear opposition
B) Permanent dictatorship
C) No elections
D) Endless coalitions only
items.correct_answer: A) A stable government and clear opposition

items.prompt:
A common disadvantage of a multi-party system is the likelihood of:

A) Complete absence of choice
B) Unstable coalition governments
C) One-man rule
D) No campaigns

The set of basic ideas and beliefs that guide a party's programme is its:

A) Inventory
B) Census
C) Ideology
D) Budget deficit

The published statement of a party's programmes and promises is its:

A) Manifest
B) Memorandum of fees
C) Mandate fund
D) Manifesto

Membership dues and donations are typical sources of:

A) Party finance
B) Court fines
C) Customs duty
D) Examination fees

An organisation that seeks to influence government without contesting elections is a:

A) Political party
B) Pressure group
C) Civil service
D) Supreme Court

mcq_options.text: Does not seek to form government

items.prompt:
The main difference between a pressure group and a political party is that a pressure group:

A) Always wins elections
B) Makes the laws
C) Does not seek to form government
D) Tries the cases
items.correct_answer: C) Does not seek to form government

items.prompt:
A trade union acting to protect workers' interests is an example of a:

A) Law court
B) Census office
C) Electoral commission
D) Pressure group

The party or group that scrutinises and criticises the ruling government is the:

A) Opposition
B) Cabinet
C) Civil service
D) Judiciary

A healthy opposition strengthens democracy mainly by:

A) Banning elections
B) Holding the government accountable
C) Printing money
D) Closing parliament

People who join and pay dues to a political party are its:

A) Witnesses
B) Defendants
C) Members
D) Tourists

Organised efforts by parties to win votes before an election are called:

A) Census
B) Trials
C) Audits
D) Campaigns

Political parties contribute to peaceful change of government by:

A) Providing organised competition for power
B) Encouraging coups
C) Banning voting
D) Abolishing the constitution
items.correct_answer: A) Providing organised competition for power

items.prompt:
A possible harm of intense party rivalry is the promotion of:

A) Free education
B) Bitterness and disunity
C) Independent courts
D) Lower prices

By aggregating diverse demands into programmes, parties perform the function of:

A) Tax collection
B) Judicial review
C) Interest aggregation
D) Coronation

Members of a political party are normally united by a shared:

A) Postal code
B) Blood type
C) Shoe size
D) Political ideology

A no-party system of government is most associated with:

A) Some traditional or military regimes
B) Vibrant multiparty democracies
C) Two-party democracies
D) Coalition cabinets
items.correct_answer: A) Some traditional or military regimes

items.prompt:
Excessive private financing of parties raises concern about:

A) Better roads
B) Undue influence on government
C) Faster trials
D) Cheaper food

A peaceful method commonly used by pressure groups is:

A) Rigging elections
B) Bribing judges
C) Lobbying and peaceful protest
D) Staging coups

In a parliamentary system, the alternative government-in-waiting is the:

A) Supreme Court
B) Census board
C) Electoral tribunal
D) Shadow cabinet

Campaign promises are mainly drawn from a party's:

A) Manifesto
B) Court record
C) Tax return
D) Census form

A party that favours gradual reform while preserving tradition is broadly:

A) Revolutionary
B) Conservative
C) Anarchist
D) Apolitical

A party that emphasises state provision of welfare and equality is broadly:

A) Conservative
B) Fascist
C) Socialist
D) Monarchist

Parties help to organise government by forming the:

A) Census and the audit
B) Army and the navy
C) Bench and the bar
D) Government and the opposition

The ultimate aim of a political party is to:

A) Win and exercise governmental power
B) Organise sports
C) Sell goods
D) Run a school only
items.correct_answer: A) Win and exercise governmental power

items.prompt:
A professional association of lawyers acting to influence policy is a:

A) Political party
B) Pressure group
C) Court of appeal
D) Census bureau

The expectation that party members vote along agreed lines is called:

A) Judicial review
B) Civil disobedience
C) Party discipline
D) Free trade

Public funding of parties is sometimes provided to reduce:

A) Voter turnout
B) Press freedom
C) Court sittings
D) Dependence on wealthy donors

Nigeria's Fourth Republic operates broadly as a:

A) Multi-party system
B) One-party system
C) No-party system
D) Monarchy

Cross-carpeting, where members switch parties for gain, can weaken:

A) The water supply
B) Party stability and ideology
C) The weather
D) The census

The opposition offers voters an important benefit by providing:

A) Free electricity
B) Lower taxes automatically
C) An alternative choice of government
D) Foreign aid
items.correct_answer: C) An alternative choice of government

items.prompt:
Choosing candidates to run for office is a party process known as:

A) Litigation
B) Coronation
C) Taxation
D) Nomination

Voters can hold a ruling party accountable by comparing its record with its:

A) Manifesto promises
B) Census figures
C) Court verdicts
D) Import duties

Door-to-door visits and rallies are common tools used during:

A) Trials
B) Campaigns
C) Audits
D) Coronations

mcq_options.text: One party wins repeatedly though others are legal

items.prompt:
A dominant-party system is one in which:
